It does this through a single facade, TaskManagementService, whose collaborators come in as domain repository interfaces (UserRepository, ProjectRepository, TaskRepository). Each rule is defined once and reused. Non-empty text validation lives in the module-level helper requireText, used by createUser, createProject, addTask and assignTask. Entity-existence checks live in the private helpers requireUser, requireProject and requireTask, and every method calls them instead of repeating repository lookups. The completion transition goes through the domain's markDone instead of setting status inline, which respects the domain abstraction. There is one minor point that falls short of a violation. addTask accepts assigneeId without running requireText on it, while assignTask does. An empty or blank ID still fails in requireUser, so the existence rule still lives in one place.
